newsitem.title: USA: GFOA urges Hill to simplify arbitrage provisions.
newsitem.headline: GFOA urges Hill to simplify arbitrage provisions.

text.p: GFOA on Wednesday urged key U.S. House and Senate panel chairs to include arbitrage rebate simplification provisions in upcoming bills to implement the historic budget agreement between Congress and the President.

The Government Finance Officers Association made the request in a two-page letter mailed to Rep. Bill Archer, R-Texas, chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee and to all other House and Senate members.
The group said that a handful of rebate relief provisions proposed by Clinton on April 14 would relieve state and local governments of burdensome regulation.
But the group said it supports some "technical" changes to the Clinton proposals and the addition of a new provision.
The new language would permit small issuers that do not have taxing authority to take advantage of a rebate exception for small issuers.
"Many governments join together to form joint authorities to respond to common needs and avoid duplication of effort," said GFOA in its letter.

"These small issuers have to incur expenses for lawyers, consultants, investment advisers, accountants and in-house staff to comply with the rebate requirement - but typically no rebate is even owed," GFOA said.

"If the same bonds were sold by a small city or county with taxing power, rather than a special district type of government, they would qualify for exemption," GFOA said. "Federal tax law should support, not penalize, consolidated governments."
